summary: E2E test of the two new AI features leveraging cv_data: (1) /api/jobs/{id}/applicant-scores endpoint used in Applications with 'Match IA' column, (2) cv_data-enriched ai_rank_candidates now powers /api/jobs/{id}/suggestions. Backend: 8/8 pytest pass (auth guards 401/403, 404 unknown job, empty dict when no applications, score-shape 0-100, suggestions still work and sorted desc). Frontend: admin login (email+password+captcha) works; Suggestions IA intro contains 'et le contenu de leurs CV'; expanding job 94d2d203... reveals 3 suggested-score-* badges ('65% compatible'); Applications page with no filter has NO 'Match IA' column; selecting 'Développeur React Senior' shows Match IA column with match-badge '80%' inside app-match-* cell; clicking the row opens dialog with detail-match-reason ('Analyse de correspondance IA — Correspondance sur les domaines.') and dialog match-badge (80%).
critical_code_review_comments: jobs.py::ai_rank_candidates — LLM call is fired synchronously on every /applicant-scores and /suggestions request; consider caching the AI ranking per (job_id, cv_data updated_at) to avoid latency (5-15s) and repeated cost when the admin flips between jobs. A short TTL (e.g. 10 min) would be enough.

jobs.py::/applicant-scores — when the LLM fails or returns nothing, a fallback score of 20 with reason 'Correspondance faible avec l'offre.' is applied for every applicant. Consider surfacing an AI-unavailable flag so the UI can differentiate LLM-derived scores from heuristic fallback.

AdminDashboard.js Applications — the effect on activeJobId depends on jobFilter, so re-selecting the same job (or switching then back) will re-fire the AI call. Combined with the backend having no cache, this is expensive; adding a client-side memo keyed by activeJobId would help.
AdminDashboard.js Applications — 'Match IA' column header text is hardcoded; consider i18n if language switcher is FR/EN (visible in header).
